c4 CLOSURE RE-VERIFICATION CATCHES TRANSITIVE HEADER CHANGES VERIFIED: extract_closure_from_parsed (certificate.py:442-478) walks parsed.tu.get_includes() (same source as build_certificate's _closure_walk), dedups by absolute path, reads each file via Path(fpath).read_bytes(), hashes -- stores (file_list, content_hash) in the cache entry. On HIT, verify_closure_content (certificate.py:416-435) re-reads the SAME cached closure_file_list and re-hashes. Because the closure_file_list captures ALL transitively-included files (including forced includes via -include, which appear in tu.get_includes() per attack #7), any transitive header content edit -- even with no macro/define change -- flips the hash and forces a safe MISS. The two-phase protocol (pre-parse bucket key + post-HIT c4 re-verification) correctly resolves the chicken-and-egg: c4 needs parsed.tu.get_includes() so it cannot be in the pre-parse bucket key, but the cached closure_file_list lets us re-verify cheaply (~0.5ms, file reads only) on HIT. Edge cases: header deleted between builds -> OSError -> False (MISS); header unreadable -> OSError -> False (MISS); new header added via -include flag -> L1 NCC argv captures it -> bucket key differs -> MISS.

DESIGN SOUNDNESS: The safety principle 'SAFE REUSE > MAXIMAL REUSE; false miss acceptable, false hit blocking' is consistently applied. Every uncertainty path fails closed to MISS. The L3 two-level cache (_L3_BUILTIN_CACHE keyed by toolchain config only; _L3_FULL_CACHE keyed by (toolchain, ncc_serial)) is a pure performance optimisation that does not affect safety. Cache is process-global, thread-safe (threading.Lock), bounded (max_entries=4096, FIFO eviction), not persisted to disk (libclang TranslationUnit objects cannot be safely serialized). Phase 2 (_process_unit) is serialised via write_lock, so concurrent access to cached parsed.tu is not an issue. Cache eviction causes MISS (re-parse) which is safe.
